claim: Bases was introduced as a new core plugin in Obsidian 1.9.0 (May 2025) in early access.
quote: Introducing Bases, a new core plugin that lets you turn any set of notes into a powerful database. Important: This is an early beta.

claim: Dataview is the most popular community plugin for querying Obsidian notes; current star count.
quote: A data index and query language over Markdown files, for https://obsidian.md/.

claim: Dataview slows large vaults, especially on mobile; Datacore is faster but uses React components that are arcane to average users; Bases is fastest and visual.
quote: Dataview… gets sluggish if you're using it with large vaults… Datacore is way faster than Dataview… arcane and cryptic to the average user… [Bases] even faster than Datacore, and without the downside of having to learn a programming language.

claim: Practical guide: singular property names, no spaces, autocomplete to avoid duplicates, restraint, and adding properties to templates.
quote: Default to singular properties whenever you can… Don't use spaces when naming your properties… Utilize autocomplete… The very best tip that I can give you when it comes to using Properties in Obsidian is to add them to your template files.

claim: Properties are YAML metadata at the top of a note; six types (text, number, list, checkbox, date, date & time); singular tag/alias/cssclass deprecated in 1.4, dropped in 1.9.
quote: Obsidian supports the following property types: Text, List, Number, Checkbox, Date, Date & time… Three singular properties were deprecated in Obsidian 1.4: tag, alias, cssclass.

claim: Tag syntax rules: alphabetical, digits, underscore, hyphen, slash for nesting; must contain at least one non-numeric character; no spaces; case-insensitive; nested tags match parents.
quote: Tags must contain at least one non-numerical character. For example, #1984 isn't a valid tag, but #y1984 is… Create nested tags by using forward slashes (/) in the tag name, for example #inbox/to-read… tag:inbox will match #inbox as well as all nested tags such as #inbox/to-read.

claim: Community consensus: tags and properties serve fundamentally similar functions, choice is preference-driven.
quote: they're both just labels you attach to your notes.

claim: Many experienced users use frontmatter tags for note-level classification (status, type) and inline tags for content-specific markers (quote, todo).
quote: Many experienced Obsidian users combine both: frontmatter for status and type (#active, #reference), inline for content-specific markers (#quote, #todo). Property tags describe the entire note.

claim: Opinionated split: folders for file type, links for navigation (not discovery), tags for 1-3 word topics with hierarchy, properties for minutiae.
quote: Use folders for the type of files contained within them… Use links for convenient navigation… not for the hope of magical serendipity… Use tags for topics that are usually 1-3 words… Properties are for minutiae.

claim: Tag sparingly, three-category taxonomy (type/status/topic), 'how will I search for this later' as the gate, restraint at creation beats pruning after.
quote: every note that has a tag needs to mean something… Tags seem to proliferate faster than they can be wrangled in… resist adding more categories until you've proven these three aren't enough.

claim: Bases renders nearly instantly even in 50k-note vaults; Dataview's grouping, TASK/CALENDAR/LIST views, and inline key::value parsing are not in Bases; migrate inline metadata to YAML first.
quote: Bases results render nearly instantly, even in my vault with over 50,0000 notes… If you currently have something like key::value in the contents of your notes, you'll need to move that data into the YAML frontmatter instead… [grouping] is one area where Dataview is still better than Bases.

claim: Bases is a core plugin offering database-like views (table, list, cards, map) backed by .base files or markdown code blocks; queries data stored in properties.
quote: Bases is a core plugin that lets you create database-like views of your notes… Bases syntax, which can be saved as a .base file or embedded in code blocks within your Markdown files.

claim: Tag Wrangler plugin enables right-click rename of tags across the entire vault.
quote: right-click a tag in the Tags view and rename it across your vault.

claim: Bases became generally available to all users (not just Catalyst) with Obsidian 1.9.10 in August 2025.
quote: As of version 1.9.10's release in August 2025, Obsidian Bases became available to everyone. Prior to this general availability rollout, the Bases feature had been in testing and was only available to Catalyst members.
